text: Basic poultry care (ការថែទាំបសុបក្សី) depends on adequate feed (ចំណីបសុបក្សី), reliable clean water, suitable shelter, ventilation, predator/weather protection, and daily observation. Grain alone is not a complete diet -- chickens and ducks need energy, protein/amino acids, minerals, and vitamins, and requirements change by stage (chicks growing fast, layers producing eggs, meat birds growing rapidly). Chicks (កូនមាន់) are especially vulnerable to cold, wet, predators, overcrowding, and feed/water competition. During the wet season, keep housing dry and manage wet litter promptly -- damp, dirty conditions raise disease and parasite risk, but don't seal the house so tightly that ventilation suffers. During the dry season, heat is the main concern -- provide shade, ventilation, and reliable water, and avoid unnecessary handling during the hottest hours. Keep feeders/drinkers clean and positioned to reduce droppings/soil contamination. A sudden drop in feed or water consumption, or in egg production, is an early warning sign worth investigating. Many Cambodian smallholders keep free-ranging or scavenging birds rather than enclosed commercial housing -- this reduces feed costs but increases exposure to wild birds, predators, and disease; do not automatically push farmers toward full confinement. Do not assume a particular chicken breed is dominant in Preah Vihear -- record the farmer's actual bird type (local/native, improved, broiler, layer, duck) rather than guessing.
